body:
**Adversarial review, round 1** on `fe6f344` by claude-opus-5-5 (builder: claude-sonnet-5-5).

request_changes: FR-004 still has an open [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] and no boundary case, so it can't be locked. The cases also never check that readings belong to the requested sensor (s-1 and s-2 have the same timestamps), so an implementation that ignores the sensor id would pass. The new endpoint is also missing from app/openapi.yaml.

- **F-1** [high] FR-004 still carries an unresolved [NEEDS CLARIFICATION], so its limit cannot be tested — `specs/1.md:19`
  The maximum range is never given, so FR-004 is not a testable requirement. The spec admits the cases only hold for 'any limit' between 1 day and about 4 years. An implementation that rejects anything over 25 hours and one that accepts up to 3 years would both pass. Nothing tests the boundary: a range exactly at the maximum, and one just over it. It is also not stated whether 'longer than' means strictly greater. Locking a spec with an open clarification hands the decision to the implementer. Pick the limit (e.g. 7 days, which fits within the 10-day fixture in app/src/data.ts), state the boundary rule, and add an exactly-at-limit 200 case and a just-over 400 case.
- **F-2** [medium] Nothing tests the 'only readings of that sensor' part of FR-001; a sensor-ignoring implementation passes — `app/cases/1/history.spec.ts:19`
  In app/src/data.ts, s-1 and s-2 both come from series(), with the same start time and the same hourly timestamps. The cases only check `at` values and `typeof value === 'number'`. An implementation that always returns s-1's readings, or returns made-up values, passes every case. That includes the s-2 case, because `sensorId` is just echoed from the path. Add an assertion that ties values to the sensor, e.g. the s-1 and s-2 values for the same range differ (base 21 vs 18), or that a value matches what /sensors/{id}/latest reports for the final hour.
- **F-3** [medium] New endpoint is left out of the contract (app/openapi.yaml) — `specs/1.md:26`
  app/openapi.yaml is the API contract, and right now it only has /sensors/{id}/latest. This spec adds a new path, a new response schema (sensorId plus a readings array) and a new 400 Error code, but says openapi.yaml 'is not changed'. After this lands, the contract and the server would disagree. Either add /sensors/{id}/history to openapi.yaml (the from/to query params, a History schema, and the 200/400/404 responses) under this spec, or say outright that contract drift is accepted and who fixes it.
- **F-4** [low] Missing negative and edge cases: empty result, error precedence, timestamp format — `app/cases/1/history.spec.ts`
  (1) No case covers a known sensor with a valid range that holds no readings, e.g. a range in 2025. FR-001 implies 200 with `readings: []`, but an implementation could return 404 and still pass. (2) The spec does not say which error wins for an unknown sensor with an over-limit range (404 or 400). (3) The cases require millisecond output ('...T02:00:00.000Z'), which is stricter than FR-001's plain 'date-time'. Either state that format in FR-001 or compare with Date.parse.


Only @dharishan04 can close a finding without a fix: `/dismiss <F-n> <reason>`.

**Adversarial review, round 2** on `a27c012` by claude-opus-5-5 (builder: claude-sonnet-5-5, claude-sonnet-5-5).

I would approve this round. All four open findings are fixed, and I checked each against app/src/data.ts, which holds 240 hourly readings per sensor starting 2026-01-01T00:00Z. s-1 values are 21 + sin(i/4)·2 and s-2 values are 18 + sin(i/4)·2.

- **F-1 (fixed):** FR-004 now sets the limit at 7 days, with `to - from > 7 days` meaning too large and exactly 7 days allowed. Both edges are tested: Jan 1 to Jan 8 returns 200 with 169 readings, all inside the data, so this also checks the inclusive `to` bound. Adding one second returns 400 `range_too_large`.
- **F-2 (fixed):** The new two-sensor test compares readings at the same timestamps. s-1 and s-2 values always differ by 3, so an implementation that ignores the sensor id but echoes `sensorId` now fails.
- **F-3 (fixed):** app/openapi.yaml now documents `/sensors/{id}/history` with a `History` schema and 200/400/404 responses that reuse `Error`. This matches FR-001 to FR-005 and the existing `latest` endpoint's style.
- **F-4 (fixed):** The empty result is tested with the 02:10 to 02:50 window, which expects `{sensorId:'s-1', readings:[]}`. Error precedence and other timestamp formats are now explicitly out of scope. No test mixes an unknown sensor with an oversized range, so nothing relies on an unstated precedence.

One new low-severity issue: the spec lists FR-006 as covered by history.spec.ts, but no test there checks openapi.yaml. It doesn't block the merge.

- **F-5** [low] FR-006 is listed as covered by history.spec.ts, but no case checks app/openapi.yaml — `specs/1.md:8`
  Both the `cases[0].covers` entry and the milestone list FR-006 under app/cases/1/history.spec.ts. None of the nine tests in that file reads or validates app/openapi.yaml, and none checks responses against the new `History` schema. FR-006 is satisfied today only because this PR edits openapi.yaml directly. Nothing would catch the contract drifting from the implementation later (for example, a renamed field or a missing 400 entry). The covers claim is false as written. Either add a case that loads openapi.yaml and checks that `/sensors/{id}/history` has 200/400/404 entries and the `History` schema, or stop listing FR-006 as covered by this case file and note that the spec PR satisfies it directly.

Re-checked and fixed: F-1, F-2, F-3, F-4
